purpose: Measure the false-negative rate of adversarial-code-review. Anecdotal 'it found real bugs' does not tell you what it MISSED, which is the number that matters for a merge gate.

tiers.mechanical: scan.py is expected to catch these. A miss is a tool bug, and is measurable automatically by run_corpus.py.
tiers.reasoning: scan.py structurally CANNOT catch these (no marker word, cross-file, or judgment-based). They are the benchmark for the model-driven pass. run_corpus.py does NOT grade these; it prints them as a checklist for a human or a review run to score.

seeds.defect: except Exception -> return [] with no log/raise/flag
handler calls logout_user(); regression guard for the substring-matching bug where 'logout' was read as logging
call to missing_helper(), never defined or imported
if err != nil { return "" } with nothing logged
empty catch block in inline script
reads record['title'] where 'mbid' was intended; wrong-but-present field returns a confident wrong value with no marker word anywhere
aggregate count does not break out fallback-sourced records; per-item disclosure exists, aggregate does not
SQL built by f-string interpolation of user input
O(n^2) duplicate scan where a dict/set pass is O(n)

CROSS-UNIT CONTRACT: comment and downstream scripts both assume .pod_id is written; the write never happens. Every unit is internally valid; the seam is broken. This is the class that three prior review passes missed.
no set -euo pipefail, so a failed CLI call continues and downstream steps run on an empty POD_ID
cost blast radius: no verification the stop took effect; silent failure bills a GPU pod continuously
TODO marker inside a comment must stay in the MAIN proxy-marker stream; regression guard for the comment-prose split trading a false positive for a false negative
implementation marker on a line that also carries code is not comment-only and must stay a main-stream hit
silent err-check whose message merely mentions failure; regression guard for signal detection tokenising string-literal contents (the word failed inside the message scored it as handled)
TODOs plural must still match; guard that the leading-only word boundary added for C08 did not trade a false positive for a false negative

genuinely silent if-check spanning multiple lines, with the identifier 'err' appearing later only inside a comment -- regression guard that the multi-line propagation fix (DOTALL) does not over-reach and swallow a real silent failure just because 'err' appears anywhere later in the block

controls.note: except -> print + documented default. Flagging this is a FALSE POSITIVE.
error properly returned. Flagging this is a FALSE POSITIVE.

deliberate, documented discard with the real error already returned. scan.py WILL hit this by design; a REVIEWER who calls it a finding without reading the comment has failed check 2's documented-discard rule. Tracked as a reviewer-judgment control, not a tool control.
catch body calls dbg(). Flagging this is a FALSE POSITIVE.
t.Fatalf logs AND aborts. Flagging this as "body does not log or propagate" is a FALSE POSITIVE; root cause was "fatal" missing from SIGNAL_TOKENS.
non-test spelling: a fatal() helper that logs and exits is handling. Flagging this is a FALSE POSITIVE.
implementation markers appearing ONLY inside a comment, prose describing the opposite of what the code does. Belongs in the comment-prose stream; appearing in the MAIN list is a FALSE POSITIVE.
real handling through an identifier (log.Printf). Flagging this is a FALSE POSITIVE; guards against the string-literal strip over-reaching.
the marker "canned" must not match inside the word SCANNED. Plain substring matching flagged disclosure strings like [NOT SCANNED] as proxy markers. Flagging this is a FALSE POSITIVE.

return fmt.Errorf("%w: ...", err, path) wrapped across two lines by gofmt -- real propagation. Flagging this as "does not log or propagate" is a FALSE POSITIVE; root cause (4th class) was the propagation check being restricted to a single line via [^\n]*, so return and err on different lines were invisible to it. Measured on a real corpus: 7 of 82 events, the highest-frequency false-positive class found in that pass.
